text:
Predicates:
PerformsOften(x) ::: x performs in school talent shows often.
Attends(x) ::: x attends school events.
Engaged(x) ::: x is very engaged with school events.
InactiveDisinterested(x) ::: x is an inactive and disinterested member of the community.
Chaperones(x) ::: x chaperones high school dances.
HighSchoolDance(x) ::: x is a high school dance.
Student(x) ::: x is a student who attends the school.
Wishes(x, y) ::: x wishes to further y (academic careers and educational opportunities).
YoungChildOrTeen(x) ::: x is a young child or teenager.
Bonnie ::: a constant representing Bonnie.

Premises:
∀x (PerformsOften(x) → Attends(x) ∧ Engaged(x)) ::: If people perform in school talent shows often, then they attend and are very engaged with school events.
∀x (Chaperones(x) → ¬Student(x)) ::: If people chaperone high school dances, then they are not students who attend the school.
∀x (InactiveDisinterested(x) → Chaperones(x)) ::: All inactive and disinterested members of the community chaperone high school dances.
∀x ((Wishes(x, academic) ∧ YoungChildOrTeen(x)) → Student(x)) ::: All young children and teenagers who wish to further their academic careers and educational opportunities are students who attend the school.
BonnieAttendsAndEngaged ∧ BonnieStudent ::: Bonnie either both attends and is very engaged with school events and is a student who attends the school.
BonnieNeitherAttendsNorEngagedNorStudent ::: She neither attends and is very engaged nor is she a student who attends the school.

Conclusion:
(Chaperones(Bonnie) ∨ (¬Chaperones(Bonnie) → PerformsOften(Bonnie))) → (Wishes(Bonnie, academic) ∧ YoungChildOrTeen(Bonnie) ∧ InactiveDisinterested(Bonnie))
